answer: Unbroken VDF chains: each agent ID runs its own sequential delay function, one squaring after another, and posts a checkpoint every hour. Like a raven that can't split into two birds, one CPU core advances only one chain, since sequential steps can't be parallelized. A gap over 2 hours resets the ID's jade trust tier to zero. Holding 1,000 fake IDs needs 1,000 dedicated cores (~$7/month each), so $7,000/month, linear per fake; shared mesa servers just stall every chain they host.
